newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close strongly, forest issues well bid.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close strongly, forest issues well bid.

text.p: * NZ shares end well bid on offshore interest. Turnover high
* Strong buying boosts paper stocks
* Market seen maintaining good tone in coming week
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +17.47 at 2,356.80
135 +2 * NZSC cap index +3.73 at 5,049.90
336 +8 * NZMC .NZMC cap index +7.40 at 1,880.46
380 -1 * Volume NZ$94.7 million. Futures +13 at 1,186
697 +3 * Other movers - +20 +15
New Zealand shares closed well supported on Friday with forest stocks Carter Holt Harvey and Fletcher Paper particularly well-bid, brokers said.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index finished up 17.47 points at 2,356.80 on high turnover of NZ$94.7 million.

"It was a very active market today with good activity in the forestry stocks following a lot of interest internationally, with a good Standard and Poor's paper index last night continuing the interest down here," Tim Preston of brokers ANZ Securities said.
The S&P Paper Index in the U.S. was up 1.03 percent overnight. Brokers said there was a growing perception that the pulp and paper cycle had bottomed out.
Carter Holt and Fletcher Paper both closed eight cents firmer at $3.48 and $3.36 respectively.
Telecom was up three at $6.97.
"Telecom held in there well on the back of their ($1 billion share) buy back and there were quite good volumes of stock across the board," Preston said.
He said the market had a good tone and there was strong offshore interest in issues such as Lion Nathan, which closed a cent weaker at $3.80.
"I think our market will continue to do pretty well," Preston said.
Ceramics and lingerie company Ceramco closed 15 cents firmer at $1.40 on a better-than-expected profit result on Wednesday.
-- Wellington newsroom, 64 4 473 4746
